text.p: The head of state-owned Lithuanian Airlines Stasys Daildyka has been sacked due the company's disappointing performance under his management, a transport ministry official said on Wednesday.
Although the company reported a modest profit last year, a transport Ministry official said the company should have done better. The company's board was also dismissed.
"The company is profitable but we anticipated greater vitality for the company and that has not been ensured by the former board of the company," the official said.
Stasys Jarmalavichius, the former deputy head of the flights department, was named to replace Dailydka.
The airline, which has share capital of 76.54 million litas, is one of 13 major state-owned companies slated for privatisation in the next two years.
The selloff plans are expected to be completed by July 1.
The ministry said the decision to replace Dailydka was also based on the need to prepare the company for privatisation.
